To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the rate of growth inhibition is not proportional to the rate of cell killing; 2) protein content of cells continues to increase in the absence of DNA synthesis; 3) the increase in protein is not due to cell division; 4) protein accumulation continues for several days after treatment; and 5) the rate of protein accumulation is not proportional to drug dose.

(a) protein synthesis in lethally damaged tumor cells can continue for several days after treatment with high doses of cis-DDP; (b) this continued protein accumulation is responsible for the continued increase in spheroids volume after treatment with cis-DDP; and (c) the continued protein accumulation in the spheroid is not related to the inhibition of cell proliferation.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein accumulation is not a reliable parameter to measure the effect of cytostatic agents.
the growth delay induced by cis-DDP in multicellular spheroid cultures is due to the inhibition of cell proliferation and not to the inhibition of protein accumulation.
protein accumulation in lethaly damaged cells is a secondary event, and not a primary event in the cytotoxic process of cis-DDP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cis-DDP-induced inhibition of spheroids growth is not due to inhibition of protein accumulation but rather to inhibition of DNA synthesis.
the inhibition of cell proliferation is a better parameter for drug effect than the inhibition of spheroids growth.
the inhibition of spheroidal growth is not a direct consequence of cell inactivation by the drug.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inhibition of protein accumulation in spheroid cells by treatment with cis-DDP is a very late effect of the drug.
the growth of multicellular spheroid tumors is not inhibited by the cytotoxic action of cis-DDP alone but also by inhibition of protein accumulation.

the inhibition of spheroidal growth after treatment with high dose cis-DDP is not due to a lack of protein synthesis in the surviving cells but rather due to the continued accumulation of protein in cells that are no longer capable of proliferation.
